mix_frequency_estimate: CHECK 90% / BET 10% at AA-class on QhJh3s 4-way OOP cold-caller 3-bet pot; AhAs combo ~CHECK 90%
reasoning:
Multiway protocol layered atop the cold-caller-checks-to-PFA backbone:

Four players means three villains behind in a 3-bet pot. The structural defaults stack:
  (1) OOP-cold-caller of 3bet → checks to PFA. Hard convention.
  (2) Multiway pot → reduces individual betting freedom because (a) sizing must work against the weakest range in the pot (CO 3bettor is strongest, BTN cold-call is loose, SB cold-call-of-3bet is tight), (b) bet leverage shrinks as fold equity per villain shrinks, (c) protection EV diffuses as 3 ranges retain >0 equity even when each is folded out.
  (3) Donk-bet in 3-bet pot multiway OOP is almost-never-correct except on hero-range-advantaged boards. QhJh3s is NOT a hero-range-advantaged board for an OOP cold-caller: it favors the CO 3-bettor (QQ+/AK/AQ density).

Multiway equity decomposition vs three balanced ranges on QhJh3s:
  - CO 3-bettor: QQ+, AK, AQs, sometimes A5s-A2s. AA has ~50-60% vs this range (loses to QQ/JJ for set, AK is 80/20 dominated, AQ is 88/12 dominated). Heads-up vs CO: ~58%.
  - BTN cold-call-of-3bet: TT-77, AQs-AJs, KQs, suited connectors 76s+, suited Ax. AA has ~70%+ vs this range.
  - SB cold-call-of-3bet: tightest construction — TT-99, AQs sometimes, suited broadways. AA has ~75% vs this.

Range-vs-range-vs-range-vs-range multiway equity for AA: roughly 45-50%. That is well above any single villain but the equity-realization penalty OOP-vs-three-villains is severe: typically 0.75-0.85 realization, putting AA's effective EV-equity at ~38-42%. That is enough to want to play for stacks but NOT enough to lead-bet OOP into 3 ranges that contain stronger-than-AA equity (set of Q, set of J, set of 3, QJ for two pair).

The check-raise line vs CO range-cbet on QhJh3s is HIGH-EV: CO cbets ~70% at small sizing → hero raises ~3x → fold equity vs BTN/SB nonzero, fold equity vs CO ranges (AK without heart, AQ without heart) is high, and we build pot vs the hands we're ahead of. The donk line gives up this leverage and bets into 3 unknown ranges.

Protection-vs-FD argument is the only honest defense of BET. AhAs blocks the nut heart FD (Ah = nut blocker). But this CUTS BOTH WAYS: blocking heart-FD combos means there are FEWER heart-FD-holding hands in villains' ranges that we are denying equity to. Specifically, BTN/SB's heart-FD combos are at most KhTh, ThXh-suited, 9hXh-suited; CO 3-bettor's heart-FD combos are at most AhKh, AhQh, KhQh. Hero's Ah crosses out AhKh, AhQh from CO entirely (3 combos) and reduces Khxh/etc combos in BTN/SB. Net: hero is blocking roughly 30-40% of the FD-class combos villains hold. The 'protect equity from FDs' argument is therefore HALF-strength for AhAs vs the no-Ah AA combos.

The shallow SPR (~1.8) is sometimes used to argue 'just get it in now' but at SPR 1.8 you have one bet left after a cbet, and check-raise → call → river-jam is a cleaner stack-getting line than donk → 3 callers → turn play multiway. Donking actually muddles the SPR-1.8 stack-getting math because hero is committing chips OOP-into-3 with no flow control.

Cluster note: this verdict will apply uniformly to 072/090/099/109 (all AA cold-caller OOP 3bet pots multiway, all 2-tone Jx or Q-J-x boards) because the structural posture (cold-caller checks to PFA OOP multiway 3bet pot) is identical across all 4 spots. Board texture details (2-tone hearts vs spades, 6h vs 3s as bottom card, 2h vs Qh as top) do NOT change the structural verdict — they would only modulate the minority BET frequency (~5-15% at class level).

Verdict: CHECK at HIGH confidence. The consensus BET 66% is a clear structural error: violation of cold-caller-checks-to-PFA + ignores Ah-blocker dampening protection EV + bet sizing too large for multiway protection (66% is value-bet sizing, not protection sizing).
